project.name: PrismSpace Agent Orchestration
current_orchestration_flow: Frontend sends objective, provider, model, max_agents, human_in_loop, and chat_history
Hive-style runtime plans and logs a multi-agent execution
Result is streamed and displayed in the Agent Swarm UI

main_output_model.technical_name: Context-Aware Multi-Agent Routing and Planning Model
main_output_model.purpose: A policy layer above existing LLM providers that decides task type, sub-agents, tools, provider/model, agent count, validation strategy, human approval, and final response strategy.
main_output_model.important_note: This model does not replace GPT, Claude, Gemini, NVIDIA, Groq, or other LLMs. It sits above them as an orchestration brain.

recommended_model_files.purpose: Router for selecting specialized agents or MCP tools
Neural reward/evaluator model trained from feedback
Policy rules, DAG strategy, thresholds, and routing configuration

2024_or_newer_methods: Embedding classifier using BGE-M3 or E5-Mistral-style embeddings
orchestration_functions.use_case: Classify request as code, Figma, GitHub, browser, database, research, mixed workflow, and similar task types.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: Sentence embeddings plus a lightweight classifier such as Logistic Regression, XGBoost, or LightGBM.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Select Planner, Code Agent, Figma Agent, GitHub Agent, Filesystem Agent, Browser Agent, Database Agent, Research Agent, Validation Agent, or MCP tools.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: Embedding retrieval over tool/agent descriptions plus a cross-encoder or LLM reranker.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Choose OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, NVIDIA, or another provider based on quality, cost, latency, task type, and past success.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: Contextual bandit or supervised router trained from task metadata and result quality.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Convert user objectives into multi-agent DAGs: plan, execute, validate, retry, evolve.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: LLM-generated JSON DAG with validation rules and deterministic execution.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Predict whether an agent run will fail, exceed budget, need human approval, or require more agents.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: XGBoost or LightGBM over telemetry: task type, provider, model, tool count, retry count, latency, errors, and cost.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Learn from human approvals, rejected outputs, edited responses, task success, and failed runs.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: Pairwise preference dataset from accepted versus rejected agent outputs.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Learn when to spawn more agents, retry, ask the user, call tools, validate, or stop.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: Start with contextual bandits before full PPO or online RL.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Detect stuck agents, repeated tool failures, high token burn, strange latency, failed loops, and abnormal logs.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: Rules plus Isolation Forest over run telemetry.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Group similar user tasks and discover reusable agent workflow templates.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: Embed objectives and successful DAGs, cluster with HDBSCAN, then label clusters with an LLM.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Retrieve previous runs, project docs, memory, similar workflows, tool examples, and file context.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: Hybrid BM25 plus vector search with reranking.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Predict token cost, latency, number of tool calls, and number of workers needed.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: XGBoost or LightGBM regression with uncertainty estimates.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Decide whether a task needs human approval for file writes, GitHub actions, external APIs, expensive tasks, or destructive operations.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: Rule-based risk labels plus calibrated classifier.

orchestration_functions.use_case: Combine outputs from multiple agents or models and pick/refine the best final answer.
orchestration_functions.practical_start: Generate candidates from multiple agents, score with evaluator, refine final output.

datasets_evaluated.name: LARK-Lab/EnvFactory-SFT-FILTERED

datasets_evaluated.name: LARK-Lab/EnvFactory-RL
datasets_evaluated.notes: Contains tool-use trajectories, tool calls, tool responses, and reward signals.

datasets_evaluated.name: ICIP/LiveMCPBench
datasets_evaluated.notes: Benchmark includes real-world MCP tasks, MCP servers, and many tools for evaluating agents.

datasets_evaluated.name: ScaleAI/lhaw
datasets_evaluated.notes: LHAW transforms well-specified tasks into underspecified variants across goals, constraints, inputs, and context.

datasets_evaluated.name: Bordair/bordair-multimodal
datasets_evaluated.recommendation: Recommended for guardrails, not main orchestration training
datasets_evaluated.notes: Useful before enabling MCP tools, file writes, browser automation, or GitHub actions.

datasets_evaluated.name: EtaYang10th/Open-M3-Bench
datasets_evaluated.recommendation: Use only if adding multimodal/image agents
datasets_evaluated.notes: Less important for current text/code/tool orchestration unless vision agents are added.

datasets_evaluated.name: MAI-UI Technical Report
datasets_evaluated.recommendation: Use as architecture reference, not as a dataset
datasets_evaluated.notes: A model/system definition paper rather than a direct dataset for this project.

recommended_dataset_order.name: RL

suggested_training_pipeline: Create run logs from PrismSpace/Hive: objective, selected agents, selected tools, provider/model, max_agents, latency, token cost, errors, user approvals, final result.
Fine-tune or train a lightweight tool-use/router model using EnvFactory-SFT-FILTERED.
Add prompt-injection guardrails using Bordair multimodal.
Use EnvFactory-RL only after SFT and telemetry are stable.
Store orchestration thresholds and policy in orchestration_policy.json.
Deploy lightweight .joblib routers first, then add .safetensors reward or neural routing models later.

recommended_first_build: Embedding similarity plus rules for routing
XGBoost or LightGBM for success prediction and cost prediction
GraphRAG or hybrid retrieval for memory
Reward model later after collecting human feedback
